catalyst_text: Positive Phase 1 data and Phase 2 initiated
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline Phase 1 results for subcutaneous B-cell depletion therapy in AChR-antibody-positive myasthenia gravis were reported from 11 patients, with 82% achieving MG-ADL MCID and a mean 4.6-point improvement at Week 24. A Phase 2 trial was also initiated to evaluate maintenance therapy following a single induction cycle of efgartigimod in adult MG. These milestones advance the program into Phase 2 and support potential for durable disease control with reduced treatment burden.
catalyst_text_evidence: TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:TGTX) (the "Company" or "TG Therapeutics"), today announced positive topline Phase 1 data for BRIUMVI in patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) and the initiation of a Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating BRIUMVI as a maintenance therapy following induction with efgartigimod in adult patients with MG. At Week 24, 82% of patients achieved the Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) in MG-ADL, defined as a decrease of ≥ 2, with a median time to MCID of 30 days. Overall, a mean 4.6 point improvement in MG-ADL was observed at Week 24. A Phase 2 trial has been initiated to evaluate the efficacy and safety of BRIUMVI in maintaining clinical response in patients with myasthenia gravis (MG) who initially respond to treatment with the FcRn inhibitor efgartigimod.

catalyst_text: Announced positive Phase 1 data topline results expected
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive Phase 1 pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, and tolerability data were reported for the investigational subcutaneous formulation compared with the approved intravenous regimen in relapsing multiple sclerosis. The data showed >60% bioavailability, consistent B-cell depletion, and a tolerability profile without new safety signals, supporting the dosing regimens being evaluated in Phase 3.
catalyst_text_evidence: TG Therapeutics, Inc. today announced positive pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), safety, and tolerability data from its Phase 1 clinical trial evaluating subcutaneous formulation of ublituximab (the active agent in BRIUMVI®) as compared to IV BRIUMVI. Subcutaneous BRIUMVI demonstrated mean bioavailability of greater than 60% relative to IV administration, with the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval exceeding 55%. Treatment with subcutaneous BRIUMVI resulted in B-cell depletion consistent with IV BRIUMVI, supporting the biological activity of the subcutaneous formulation. Subcutaneous administration was generally well tolerated, with treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) consistent with the known safety profile of IV BRIUMVI. No serious injection-site reactions and no new safety signals were observed.

catalyst_text: Phase 3 trial met primary bioequivalence endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the Phase 3 ENHANCE trial in adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis showed bioequivalence between a single 600 mg Day 1 initiation infusion and the approved split-dose initiation. Safety and tolerability were consistent with prior studies, with no new safety signals and fewer infusion reactions observed with the single-infusion regimen. These findings support a streamlined initiation that could eliminate the Day 15 infusion visit.
catalyst_text_evidence: 2026-05-27 -- TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:TGTX), today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 ENHANCE trial, a randomized, double-blind study evaluating a consolidated single infusion regimen for initiation of BRIUMVI (ublituximab-xiiy) in adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS). The trial met its primary endpoint, demonstrating bioequivalent drug exposure between the currently approved initiation dosing regimen of 150 mg on Day 1 and 450 mg on Day 15 and a consolidated single 600 mg infusion on Day 1, eliminating the need for a Day 15 infusion. Secondary endpoints, including safety, B-cell depletion, and MRI outcomes, were consistent with prior BRIUMVI clinical studies and comparable between treatment arms through the primary assessment period with no new safety signals observed. Infusion-related reactions in both arms were lower than previously reported in the ULTIMATE I and II approval studies for BRIUMVI, with no Grade 3 or higher infusion reactions occurring in either arm.

catalyst_text: Announced positive results to be presented at CMSC
detailed_catalyst_text: New analyses from the Phase 4 ENABLE study in adults with relapsing multiple sclerosis showed significant and durable improvements in patient-reported outcomes, with benefits evident by Day 15 and sustained through Week 48. Real-world transition data reported 99.4% of patients remained relapse-free with an annualized relapse rate of 0.011, alongside improved convenience and tolerability, with presentation materials available online.

catalyst_text: Presented positive real world and dosing data
detailed_catalyst_text: New clinical data for BRIUMVI in adults with relapsing multiple sclerosis were presented at AAN 2026, including real-world findings from the ENABLE Phase 4 observational study and dosing regimen updates from ENHANCE. These presentations add evidence on effectiveness, safety, and tolerability in routine practice and provide insights to optimize intravenous dosing, supporting broader clinical use.
